## Understanding Quarto Listings

### What are Quarto Listings?

Quarto Listings provide an automated approach to organizing and displaying website content based on document metadata.

Rather than manually updating a portfolio whenever a new project is completed, listings allow Quarto to dynamically generate a collection of project entries during the rendering process.

This functionality is particularly useful for:

- Professional portfolios
- Academic research websites
- Marketing analytics projects
- Blogs and publications
- Data science case studies
- Project documentation

### Types of Listings

Quarto supports several listing formats depending on the intended presentation and audience.

| Listing type | Description | Recommended application |
|----|----|----|
| Default | Vertically organized content | Blogs and articles |
| Grid | Card-based visual presentation | Professional portfolios |
| Table | Structured rows and columns | Research and project directories |

This portfolio uses the grid format to create a structured and visually accessible presentation of professional projects.

## Implementing Quarto Listings

### Project Organization

Each project is maintained as an individual Quarto document within a dedicated projects directory.

``` text
M10/
├── _quarto.yml
├── index.qmd
├── cep.qmd
├── dashboard.qmd
├── customization.qmd
├── listings.qmd
├── theme.scss
├── styles.css
└── projects/
    └── Individual project documents (.qmd)
```

This structure separates website navigation, visual customization, analytical dashboards, and individual project content.

### Document Metadata

Each project document contains a YAML header that defines its title, description, and relevant categories.

For example:

``` yaml
---
title: "Credit Union Customer Insights"
description: "An interactive dashboard examining customer satisfaction and financial product awareness."
categories:
  - Marketing Analytics
  - Customer Insights
  - Data Visualization
---
```

Quarto extracts this metadata and uses it to automatically populate the portfolio listing.

### Listing Configuration

The following YAML configuration demonstrates how a grid-based listing can be implemented.

``` yaml
listing:
  id: portfolio-projects
  contents: projects
  type: grid
  grid-columns: 2
  categories: true
  sort-ui: true
  filter-ui: true
  sort: "title asc"
  fields: [title, description, categories]
```

| Configuration  | Function                           |
|----------------|------------------------------------|
| `id`           | Identifies the listing placement   |
| `contents`     | Specifies the source directory     |
| `type`         | Determines the presentation format |
| `grid-columns` | Sets the number of grid columns    |
| `categories`   | Enables category-based navigation  |
| `sort-ui`      | Enables interactive sorting        |
| `filter-ui`    | Enables search functionality       |
| `sort`         | Defines the initial sorting order  |
| `fields`       | Determines the displayed metadata  |

## Benefits for a Professional Portfolio

### Automated Content Management

New projects can be incorporated into the portfolio by adding individual Quarto documents to the projects directory and rendering the website.

This reduces manual maintenance and supports long-term portfolio development.

### Improved User Experience

Category filtering, searching, and sorting allow recruiters, employers, and other visitors to quickly identify projects relevant to their interests.

### Scalability

As additional academic, professional, and independent projects are completed, the portfolio can expand without requiring substantial changes to the website structure.

### Consistent Professional Branding

Quarto Listings integrate with the website's CSS and SCSS stylesheets, allowing project cards to maintain a consistent visual identity across the portfolio.
